"In the beginning, God created." What does it mean to you that everything begins with God?
Again and again God speaks and it is so, and he sees that it is good. What does this show about God's word and his world?
God made people in his image. How does this change how you see yourself and others?
God saw everything he had made, and it was very good. What in creation makes you praise God?
God rested on the seventh day and blessed it. How do you make room for rest?
God formed man from dust and breathed life into him. What does this tell you about where your life comes from?
God gave work, freedom and one boundary in the garden. What does this show about God's good design?
"It is not good that the man should be alone." What does this show about our need for one another?
The serpent asked, "Did God actually say?" How does doubt about God's word lead us astray?
Adam and Eve hid and blamed others. Why do we hide from God or shift blame?
Sin brought pain and broken relationships. Where do you see the effects of sin around you?
God promises an offspring who will crush the serpent's head. How does this point to Jesus?
God clothed Adam and Eve before sending them out. What does this show about God's care even in judgement?
God told Cain that sin was crouching at the door, but he must rule over it. What sin is crouching at your door?
Cain asked, "Am I my brother's keeper?" How would you answer that question?
God put a mark on Cain to protect him. What does this show about God's mercy?
People began to call on the name of the Lord. What does it mean for you to call on his name?
God made man and woman and blessed them. How does God's blessing shape your view of people?
The refrain "and he died" repeats again and again. What does this show about the effects of sin?
"Enoch walked with God." What would it look like for you to walk with God?
Lamech hoped Noah would bring relief from the curse. Where do you long for God's relief?
The Lord was grieved that the wickedness of people was great. What does God's grief show about his heart?
"Noah found favour in the eyes of the Lord." What does this show about grace?
Noah was righteous and walked with God in a corrupt world. How can you stay faithful when those around you don't?
Noah did all that God commanded him. What is God asking you to do?
God told Noah to go into the ark. What does God's call to safety show about his care?
"The Lord shut him in." What comfort is there in God shutting Noah in?
The waters covered the earth, but the ark floated. How has God carried you through overwhelming times?
"God remembered Noah." What does it mean to you that God remembers you?
Noah sent out the dove and waited. What are you waiting on God for?
God told Noah to go out of the ark. What new beginning might God be calling you to?
Noah built an altar and worshipped. How do you respond to God after he brings you through?
God blessed Noah and told him life is precious. Why does God value human life so highly?
God set his bow in the clouds as a sign of his covenant. What promise of God do you need to remember?
Even Noah failed after the flood. What does this teach about our need for a better Saviour?
The nations spread out across the earth from Noah's sons. What does this show about God's care for all peoples?
Nimrod became a mighty man. What makes someone great in God's eyes?
All the nations are part of one family. How should this shape how you see people from other nations?
The people wanted to make a name for themselves. Where are you tempted to build your own name?
God confused their language and scattered them. Why did God stop their plan?
The family line narrows down to Abram. What does this show about God working through ordinary families?
Sarai was barren. How does God often work through what seems impossible?
God promises to bless Abram and through him all the families of the earth. How does this point to Jesus?
Abram went as the Lord told him, not knowing everything. What step of faith is God asking of you?
Fear led Abram to lie about Sarai. When does fear tempt you to compromise?
God protected Sarai despite Abram's failure. What does this show about God's faithfulness?
Abram returned to where he had first called on the Lord. Where do you go to call on the Lord again?
Abram let Lot choose first to keep peace. When can you give up your rights for peace?
Lot chose land that looked good but was near Sodom. How do our choices reveal our hearts?
God promised Abram all the land he could see. How does God's generosity compare with what we grab for ourselves?
Abram rescued Lot even after Lot had chosen the better land. What does this show about loyalty?
Melchizedek blessed Abram, and Abram gave him a tenth. What does Abram's response show about his heart?
Abram refused the king of Sodom's riches. Why do you think he refused?
"Fear not, Abram, I am your shield; your reward shall be very great." What does this promise mean to you?
Abram believed the Lord, and he counted it to him as righteousness. What promise of God do you need to believe?
God made a covenant and passed between the pieces alone. What does this show about who keeps the covenant?
God promised the land to Abram's offspring. How has God kept his promises in your life?
Sarai tried to get God's promise by her own plan. Where are you tempted to take matters into your own hands?
The angel found Hagar by a spring in the wilderness. What does this show about God seeing the overlooked?
Hagar called God "the God who sees me." How does it feel to know God sees you?
Ishmael was born, but he was not the promised son. What does this teach about waiting for God's timing?
God said, "I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be blameless." What does walking before God look like?
God changed Abram's name to Abraham, father of many nations. What does a new name signify?
Abraham laughed at the promise of a son in old age. When have God's promises seemed too good to be true?
Abraham obeyed that very day. How quickly do you respond when God speaks?
Abraham welcomed three visitors with generous hospitality. How can you show hospitality?
"Is anything too hard for the Lord?" What situation do you need to bring to God with this question?
God shared his plans with Abraham, his friend. What does it mean to be a friend of God?
Abraham pleaded for Sodom again and again. Who could you pray for persistently?
Lot welcomed the angels while the city was wicked. What does this show about living in a corrupt place?
Lot lingered, but the Lord was merciful and brought him out. When has God been merciful when you hesitated?
Lot's wife looked back. What might you be tempted to look back to?
"God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out." How do the prayers of others matter?
Abraham repeated his old lie out of fear. What old patterns do you fall back into?
Abimelech feared God more than Abraham expected. Why might we underestimate others?
Abraham prayed for Abimelech and God healed. How can you pray for those you have wronged or been wronged by?
The Lord did to Sarah as he had promised. Sarah said, "God has made laughter for me." What has God done that brought you joy?
God told Abraham to listen and trust him about Ishmael. What hard thing do you need to trust God with?
God heard the boy crying and opened Hagar's eyes to see a well. Where do you need God to open your eyes?
Abraham called on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God. What does it mean that God is everlasting?
Abraham said, "God will provide for himself the lamb." How does this point forward to Jesus?
Abraham named the place "The Lord will provide." How has God provided for you?
Because Abraham did not withhold his son, God blessed him. What might God be asking you to hold with open hands?
Abraham mourned and wept for Sarah. How does faith make room for grief?
Abraham bought a burial plot in the land, a sign of trust in God's promise. How do you act on God's promises now?
The cave became the first piece of the promised land Abraham owned. What does this small beginning show?
Abraham trusted the Lord to send his angel ahead. Where do you need God to go ahead of you?
The servant prayed specifically and watched for God's answer. How can you pray like this?
The servant bowed and worshipped when God led him. How do you respond when God guides you?
Rebekah said, "I will go." What would it take for you to say "I will go" to God?
Abraham died "an old man and full of years." What does a faithful life look like at its end?
Isaac prayed for Rebekah, and the Lord answered. What are you praying for that you need to keep praying?
Esau despised his birthright for a bowl of stew. What lasting things might you trade for short-term wants?
God told Isaac to stay in the land and promised to be with him. Where do you need God's presence to stay put?
Isaac repeated his father's lie. How do family patterns shape us?
Isaac kept digging new wells despite quarrels. How do you respond when conflict arises?
God said, "Fear not, for I am with you." What does this mean for you today?
Rebekah and Jacob plotted to deceive Isaac. What happens when we try to get God's blessing our own way?
Jacob lied repeatedly to his father. What does this show about the slippery slope of deception?
Esau wept bitterly. How does deception hurt families?
Rebekah had to send away the son she loved. What are the consequences of sin, even when God's plan continues?
God appeared to Jacob as he fled, promising to be with him. How does God meet us even when we have failed?
Jacob said, "Surely the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it." Where might God be present that you haven't noticed?
Jacob made a vow to God. What commitment might God be inviting you to make?
Jacob met Rachel and wept for joy. What does this story show about God guiding Jacob?
The deceiver Jacob was deceived by Laban. What does this teach about reaping what we sow?
Leah named her fourth son Judah, saying, "This time I will praise the Lord." Where can you choose praise in disappointment?
Rachel envied Leah. How does envy affect relationships?
"God remembered Rachel... and opened her womb." What does this show about God's timing?
Jacob prospered despite Laban's tricks. How did God take care of Jacob?
God told Jacob, "Return... and I will be with you." Where might God be calling you to return?
Jacob saw that God had been with him despite Laban's unfairness. How has God been with you in unfair situations?
Jacob said if God had not been on his side, he would have been sent away empty. How has God been on your side?
Laban and Jacob made a covenant, saying, "The Lord watch between you and me." How can God help in strained relationships?
Jacob was greatly afraid of meeting Esau. What are you afraid of facing?
Jacob prayed, "I am not worthy of the least of all the steadfast love." How does humility change our prayers?
Jacob wrestled with God and would not let go without a blessing. What are you wrestling with God about?
God renamed Jacob as Israel. What does a new name from God mean?
Esau ran to meet Jacob and embraced him. What does this reconciliation show you?
Jacob said seeing Esau's face was like seeing the face of God. How can forgiveness reflect God's grace?
Jacob built an altar and called it "God, the God of Israel." What does it mean for God to be your God?
Dinah was badly wronged. How does God's heart respond to injustice?
Simeon and Levi answered evil with violent revenge. Why is revenge never the answer?
Jacob told his household to put away their foreign gods. What do you need to put away?
God renewed his promises to Jacob at Bethel. How has God renewed his promises to you?
Rachel died giving birth, and Isaac died old and full of days. How does faith hold through loss?
Esau's family moved away because the land couldn't support both. What does this show about God's provision for both brothers?
Esau's line is listed in detail. What does it show that God remembers every family?
Kings reigned in Edom before any king in Israel. What does this show about God's timing?
Jacob loved Joseph more than his other sons. How does favouritism damage families?
Joseph's dreams made his brothers hate him more. How can we handle the gifts God gives with humility?
Joseph's brothers sold him. How could God still be at work in such betrayal?
Jacob refused to be comforted. How do you walk with someone in deep grief?
Judah failed to do right by Tamar. What does this show about Judah's character at this point?
Judah said, "She is more righteous than I." What does it take to admit we're wrong?
Perez, born from this story, became an ancestor of Jesus. What does this show about God's grace?
"The Lord was with Joseph." How did that show in his life?
Joseph said, "How can I do this great wickedness and sin against God?" How can this help you in temptation?
Joseph did right and still ended up in prison. How do you keep trusting God when doing right costs you?
Even in prison the Lord showed Joseph steadfast love. Where do you need to see God's love in a hard place?
Joseph noticed the troubled faces of others. How can you notice those around you?
Joseph said, "Do not interpretations belong to God?" How do you give God credit?
Joseph faithfully told both the good and the bad news. How can you be truthful with kindness?
The cupbearer forgot Joseph. How do you keep trusting God when people forget you?
Joseph said, "It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh a favourable answer." How can you point to God instead of yourself?
God revealed what was coming so Pharaoh could prepare. How does God's wisdom help us plan?
Joseph went from prison to palace. What does this show about God's timing?
Joseph named his sons to remember that God made him forget his hardship and fruitful in affliction. How has God made you fruitful in hard times?
Joseph's brothers bowed before him, fulfilling his dream. How does God keep his word over many years?
The brothers said, "We are guilty concerning our brother." How does guilt work on a conscience?
Jacob said, "All this has come against me," not knowing God was at work. When have you misread God's work in your life?
Jacob let Benjamin go, saying, "May God Almighty grant you mercy." What do you need to entrust to God?
The steward told the brothers, "Peace to you, do not be afraid." How can you bring peace to anxious people?
Joseph was overcome with emotion when he saw Benjamin. What does this show about Joseph's heart?
The silver cup was found in Benjamin's sack. How did this test the brothers' hearts?
Judah said, "God has found out the guilt of your servants." What does true confession sound like?
Judah offered himself in Benjamin's place. How does Judah's change point to Jesus?
Joseph wept aloud and revealed himself. What does his weeping show?
Joseph said, "It was not you who sent me here, but God." How can you see God's hand in your past?
Joseph forgave and embraced his brothers. Who might God be asking you to forgive?
Jacob's spirit revived when he heard Joseph was alive. What brings your spirit back to life?
God told Jacob, "Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt... I myself will go down with you." Where do you need God's presence in a new place?
All of Jacob's family went down to Egypt. What does it mean that God was keeping his promise through a family?
Jacob and Joseph embraced and wept. What does reunion teach about God's restoring work?
Jacob blessed Pharaoh. What does it show that the man of God blessed the powerful king?
Joseph wisely managed the famine and saved lives. How can you use wisdom to serve others?
Jacob asked to be buried in the promised land. How does hope in God's promise shape our final wishes?
Jacob remembered how God appeared to him and blessed him. What do you remember about God's work in your life?
Jacob spoke of "the God who has been my shepherd all my life long." How has God shepherded you?
Jacob crossed his hands to bless the younger. How does God often surprise us in whom he chooses?
Jacob's words to Reuben, Simeon and Levi remember their failures. How do our actions shape our future?
Judah is promised a ruler and the obedience of the peoples. How does this point to Jesus?
Joseph's arms were made strong by the Mighty One of Jacob, the Shepherd. Where do you need God's strength?
Jacob blessed each son and then died. What blessing would you want to pass on?
Joseph mourned his father deeply. How does honouring our parents look in grief?
The brothers feared Joseph would now take revenge. Why do people struggle to believe forgiveness is real?
"You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good." Where can you see this truth in your life?
Joseph trusted God would bring them up out of Egypt. What promise of God do you hold to for the future?
